title: Accuracy of a respiratory assessment chatbot in a nationwide messaging system for layperson diagnosis and triage: a randomized preregistered study
source_used: Nature Health (journal page: full abstract, data and disclosure sections; paper body is behind subscription), from fulltext/C10-03.txt
key_facts: A peer-reviewed study in Nature Health tested LungDiag, a task-limited chatbot on WeChat built on GPT-4o with a respiratory knowledge layer, against ordinary mobile web search.
It was a prospective, multicentre, single-blind, randomized, preregistered comparison using simulated cases; AI-assisted search tools were switched off in the web-search (control) group.
Between April and June 2025, 2,400 adults with no formal medical training at 24 Chinese healthcare systems were assigned 1:1; 2,176 questionnaires (1,088 per group) entered the main analysis.
Model-based overall accuracy was 70.0% with LungDiag against 55.4% with web search, a difference of 14.6 percentage points (P < 0.001).
Diagnosis items: 81.2% against 54.5%; triage items improved less: 53.4% against 47.1%; LungDiag users took longer (median 527 seconds against 461).
For high-urgency triage, sensitivity and specificity were 85.6% and 62.1% with LungDiag against 80.9% and 56.0% with web search.
The authors state the findings do not establish effects on real-world care-seeking, diagnostic delay or clinical outcomes.

The respiratory knowledge resource is owned and maintained by the authors' research group (disclosed in the paper); the authors report no personal financial interest in it. Funding: Guangzhou National Laboratory and Chinese national and provincial science foundations.
quote_evidence: LungDiag improved simulated case-question answering among lay participants, particularly for preliminary diagnostic recognition; however, these findings do not establish effects on real-world care-seeking, diagnostic delay or clinical outcomes.
The largest difference was observed for diagnosis items (81.2% versus 54.5%), whereas triage gains were smaller (53.4% versus 47.1%).

Between April and June 2025, 2,400 adults without formal medical training at 24 Chinese healthcare systems were randomly assigned 1:1 to LungDiag assistance or browser-based search, with dedicated AI and generative AI-assisted search functions disabled in the control arm.
why_it_matters_hint: Peer-reviewed randomized evidence that a purpose-built chatbot beat web search at lay diagnosis of lung conditions in simulated cases, with no proof yet of real-world benefit.
